target.title: fix(browser): stop agent-launched managed Chrome
target.body:
Closes #109678

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running `openclaw browser stop` after an agent launched managed Chrome could still see `running: true` while the Chrome process and CDP listener remained alive.

## Why This Change Was Made

The stop transition now recovers a local managed Chrome that was launched by another browser runtime, while staying inside the profile lifecycle transition so later starts cannot race ahead of cleanup. It closes only a process proven to match the current-host singleton lock, configured executable, exact CDP port and user-data-dir arguments, process start identity, and listening socket; attach-only and remote profiles remain disconnect-only.

## User Impact

`openclaw browser stop` can now stop the same managed Chrome regardless of whether the CLI/Gateway process or an agent-side browser runtime retained the original launch handle. External and remote browsers are not terminated.

## Evidence

- Regression-first proof on current main: the two new cases failed because the cross-runtime stop helper was absent and `stopRunningBrowser()` returned `stopped: false`.
- Focused browser lifecycle suite: 5 files passed, 108 tests passed via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`.
- Targeted `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` passed for all four changed files.
- Fresh pre-commit autoreview reported no accepted/actionable findings.
- Full `check:changed` was not run locally: Blacksmith Testbox was unavailable because this machine is not authenticated to the `openclaw` organization.
- Initial pull request checks: Real behavior proof, Security Sensitive Guard, Auto response, Dependency Guard detection, and ClawSweeper dispatch passed. Labeler failed while GitHub refused its repository-content request with `fail-fast:network`; Dependency Guard enforcement and one security detection checkout were cancelled before code execution by the same trusted-base checkout/network problem. Fork contributors cannot rerun these admin-owned workflows.

### Real macOS behavior proof

Ran the built `openclaw.mjs` from commit `7ec1917` against Google Chrome on macOS with an isolated state directory and redacted ephemeral Gateway credentials. A separate agent-runtime process launched the managed profile and retained its launch handle; the Gateway and `openclaw browser stop` ran in different processes.

```text
REAL_MACOS_PROOF OpenClaw=2026.7.2 commit=7ec1917
AGENT_MANAGED_BEFORE pid=20009 cdp=60698 process=ALIVE listener=LISTEN
CLI_STOP_MANAGED exit=0 profile=managed-proof running=false cdpReady=false
AGENT_MANAGED_AFTER pid=20009 process=EXITED cdp=60698 listener=CLOSED

ATTACH_ONLY_BEFORE pid=20165 cdp=60699 process=ALIVE listener=LISTEN
CLI_STOP_ATTACH_ONLY exit=0 profile=attach-proof running=true cdpReady=true
ATTACH_ONLY_AFTER pid=20165 process=ALIVE cdp=60699 listener=LISTEN
PROOF_RESULT PASS tokens=REDACTED state=ISOLATED
```

The attach-only Chrome was terminated explicitly only during proof cleanup.
